page: OVHcloud r3-128-flex is a memory-optimized virtual instance deployed on KVM hypervisors. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture, it features 16 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. The compute subsystem is equipped with 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache pool. Total system memory measures 128.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy computing patterns.

The server includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without an integrated hardware GPU. Network interfaces deliver a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The platform supports standard x86 extensions including AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though advanced extensions such as AVX-512 are not enabled.

Benchmark results demonstrate notable memory subsystem performance. In uncached large-block throughput tests, the server recorded 245.98 GB/sec in read operations and 123.44 GB/sec in write operations, placing in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Multi-threaded decompression reached 210.8 GB/sec via bzip3, supported by strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests. General multi-core throughput, static web serving (15.77 GB/sec), and in-memory cache operations (37.0 million Redis SET operations per second) scored in the median range.

The high memory-to-vCPU density makes this configuration cost-effective for caching layers, in-memory analytics, and large operational datasets where per-gigabyte RAM allocation is prioritized over dense storage footprints. Workloads requiring expansive local storage will encounter tradeoffs due to the modest 50 GB NVMe allocation, positioning the instance primarily toward in-memory databases, memory-constrained batch jobs, and enterprise application runtimes.
